h: Doors open, people walking in, lights coming on.
steps: Stand at the back corner, phone upright, dead still — lean it on something if you can.
Press record 30 seconds before the doors open.
Let people walk through the frame. Don't follow anyone, don't direct anyone.
dont: Don't ask anyone to wave. Natural beats staged every time.

h: A real hands-on coaching moment, one member, one cue.
steps: Film from the side so the squat depth is visible.
Get your hands and the member in the same frame.
Hold for a slow count of 20 — the fix IS the story. Say the cue out loud.
dont: Don't interrupt a set to re-shoot. Catch the next one.

h: Hands clapping chalk before a big lift.
steps: Wipe your camera lens first — ten seconds, changes everything.
Get within a metre. Hands should FILL the screen.
Record a 3-count before the clap so we have a lead-in. Keep the bar in the background.
dont: Don't use slow-mo — we do that in the edit.

h: The 10 seconds after a personal best lands.
steps: When someone's going for a PB, quietly start filming early.
Keep the lifter AND whoever's cheering in one frame.
Let it run — the moment after the bar drops is the gold.
dont: Don't cut the clip the second the lift finishes.

h: Today's session on the board, marker in hand.
steps: Film yourself writing the last two lines of the session.
Get the marker sound — audio matters here.
Finish on the full board and hold for 5 seconds.
dont: Don't film an empty board — the writing is the shot.

h: Two or three members talking, laughing, resting.
steps: Film from across the room — long lens feel, unnoticed.
30 seconds minimum so there's room to cut.
Faces and laughter beat perfect framing every time.
dont: Don't get close enough to change the vibe.

h: A first-timer being shown around, first warm-up.
steps: Ask them once at the start: 'ok if we film a bit? It's for our socials.'
Catch the walk-around / handshake moment.
Then their first exercise attempt — nerves and all. That's the relatable bit.
dont: Don't film anyone who hasn't said yes.

h: End-of-class effort — sled, bike, whatever hurts.
steps: Get low — kneel at the end of the lane, phone steady.
Let them work TOWARD the camera. Stop before they reach you.
Two or three reps from the same spot is plenty.
dont: Don't stand anywhere they'll have to swerve around you.

h: Post-session shake, logo visible if you've got merch.
steps: Counter height, logo facing the phone.
Film the scoop, the shake, the first sip.
Under 30 seconds all up.
dont: Don't stage it with someone who doesn't actually drink them.

h: You teaching one movement from setup to finish.
steps: Side-on, whole body in frame, bar or bell visible.
Teach the full setup — feet, grip, brace, go.
Say the one-line cue you use every single time. That line is the hook.
dont: Don't zoom mid-clip — pick a frame and hold it.

h: One member, one question: 'why do you keep coming back?'
steps: Quiet corner, gym visible behind them, light on their face.
Ask the question OFF camera — they answer to you, not the lens.
One take is enough. Real beats polished.
dont: Don't hand them a script. Ever.

h: The room at rest — racks, chalk dust, quiet.
steps: Slow 10-second walk down the middle, phone chest-height and steady.
One take at open, one at close — send both.
Let the room breathe. No talking.
dont: Don't tidy up first. The mess is the story.
